scope: SUBOFF with sail (AFF-3 inspired), Re=1000 laminar, piDL+appendage wetted-area normalization, mix50 friction

reference.source: Blasius flat-plate Cf at Re=1000 (same caliber as the verified bare-hull suboff_re1000)
reference.note: the ITTC-1957 / DARPA AFF-8 experimental Ct values are turbulent Re~2e6-1.2e7 and NOT applicable at Re=1000

grids.note: 0 appendage cells: this run has NO sail at all, so it is a bare-hull control, not a sail ladder

caliber_finding:
The earlier claim that the sail is 'sub-grid and unusable for L<=96' is WRONG -- it came from using a FIXED
radius instead of the correct radius_lb = 0.05831*L.  With the correct radius every resolution has a sail:
L40->6, L48->12, L52->8, L56->15 ... L88->32 cells.
HOWEVER the run's own domain formula produces ODD dimensions from L>=56 (119/127/135 for L=56/60/64),
which puts the sail on a half-cell and annihilates it (0 cells) -- that is why L60 above is a bare-hull control.
blocker:
The two grids that DO carry a sail (L48: 12 cells, L52: 8 cells) have a 4.38% inter-grid span, over the 3%
acceptance gate.  The 12-vs-8 cell staircase difference in the sail alone moves Cd by 4.4%, so the gate is
measuring the appendage voxelisation, not a converged submerged-body drag.  A defensible sail ladder needs
a resolution where the sail is >= 3-5 cells thick in BOTH ladders -- which is not reachable with the current
body-fitted domain formula on a 15 GiB card.
verdict: NOT ACCEPTED (honest block). L48 alone hits -2.78% but its pair L52 is -7.16%; the 4.38% span is dominated by sail staircasing (12 vs 8 cells), so this is not a converged validation.
